newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK court frees 11 boat people in possible test case.
newsitem.headline: HK court frees 11 boat people in possible test case.

text.p: The Hong Kong High Court on Wednesday ordered the release of 11 Vietnamese migrants from detention in a case that could affect thousands of boat people incarcerated in the territory, government radio reported.

Justice Brian Keith ruled that the four applicants and their family members had no reasonable prospect of returning to their home country, making illegal their continued detention in Hong Kong pending deportation.

The four were among thousands of boat people on whose behalf the advocacy group Refugee Concern had lodged writs of habeas corpus arguing their indefinite detention without being charged with any crime was unreasonable and illegal.
Many are believed to be ethnic Chinese considered by Hanoi to be non-nationals, or lack papers to prove their nationality.

A Refugee Concern spokesman, Rob Brooks, said the court had ruled the detention of four other applicants proper, but noted that even the partial success of his group's action could have profound effects on Hong Kong's boat people policy.
"If that's any indication of the 3,000 people who remain in detention on whose behalf this action is taken, then...perhaps 1,500 people might be released," Brook told reporters.
About 7,000 Vietnamese boat people remain in detention in Hong Kong. Most have been judged economic migrants ineligible for resettlement elsewhere as refugees, and must return home.

Hong Kong is under strong pressure from Beijing to clear the camps before the territory's return to Chinese sovereignty in mid-year. More than 15,000 last year and about 1,000 already this year have been sent home, both voluntarily and forcibly.
